archive.help: [action:resync|integrity|export|exportraw|import|importold|importraw|inspect|inspectraw|addresscheck] (host:) (phrase:) (anyphrase:true|false) (keys:) (keyuses:) (file:) (address:) (statecheck:) (logs:true|false) (maxexport:) - Resync your chain with seed phrase if necessary (otherwise wallet remains the same)
archive.fullhelp:
archive

Perform a chain or seed re-sync from an archive node or archive export file.

A chain re-sync will put your node on the correct chain.

Use a chain re-sync if your node has been offline for too long and cannot catchup. Seed Phrase is not required.

A seed re-sync will wipe the wallet, re-generate your private keys and restore your coins.

Only do a seed re-sync if you have lost your node and do not have a backup.

You can also perform checks on your archive db or archive file and check an address.

action:
    integrity : Check the integrity of your archive db. No host required.
    inspect : inspect an archive export .gzip file. If 'last:1', the file can re-sync any node from genesis.
    export : Export your archive db to a .gzip file. 
    exportraw : Export your archive db to a raw .dat file (recommended).
    resync : Use with 'host' to do a chain or seed re-sync from an archive node. 
    import : Use with 'file' to do a chain or seed re-sync using a .dat or .gzip archive file. 
    addresscheck : check your archive db for spent and unspent coins at a specific address.
    importold : Import an archive backup made by an older node version (H2 format). Use with file:
    importraw : Import a raw archive export (.raw.dat). Much faster than the H2 gzip import. Use with file:
    inspectraw : Inspect a raw archive export - its cascade and block range - without importing it. Use with file:

host: (optional) 
    ip:port of the archive node to sync from. Use with action:resync.

file: (optional) 
    name or path of the archive export gzip file to export/import/inspect.

phrase: (optional)
    To seed re-sync, enter your seed phrase in double quotes. Use with action:import or resync.
    This will replace the current seed phrase of this node. You do NOT have to do this if you still have access to your wallet.
    In this case, use action:import or resync without 'phrase' to get on the correct chain.

anyphrase: (optional)
    true or false. If you set a custom seed phrase on startup, you can set this to true. Default is false.

keys: (optional) 
    Number of keys to create if you need to do a seed re-sync. Default is 64.

keyuses: (optional) 
    How many times at most you used your keys..
    Every time you re-sync with seed phrase this needs to be higher as Minima Signatures are stateful.
    Defaults to 1000 - the max is 262144 for normal keys.

address: (optional) 
    The wallet or script address to search for in the archive. Use with action:addresscheck.
    If using a script address, also provide an address or public key in the 'statecheck' parameter.
    Use with action:addresscheck.

statecheck: (optional) 
    Data to search for in a coin's state variables.
    Combine with a script address in the 'address' parameter to search for coins locked in a contract.

logs: (optional) 
    true or false. Show detailed logs, default false.

maxexport: (optional) 
    How many blocks to export to a raw .dat file. Useful for testing purposes.

Examples:

archive action:integrity

archive action:inspect file:archiveexport-ddmmyy.gzip

archive action:exportraw file:archiveexport-ddmmyy.raw.dat

archive action:resync host:89.98.89.98:9001

archive action:import file:archiveexport-ddmmyy.raw.dat

archive action:import file:archiveexport-ddmmyy.raw.dat phrase:"YOUR 24 WORD SEED PHRASE" keyuses:2000

archive action:addresscheck address:0xFED.. statecheck:0xABC..

archive action:importraw file:archivebackup.raw.dat

archive action:inspectraw file:archivebackup.raw.dat

coins.fullhelp:
coins

Search for coins that are relevant to you or in the unpruned chain.

relevant: (optional)
    true or false, true will only return coins you are tracking.
    false will search all coins in the unpruned chain.
    Default is false unless no other parameters are provided.

sendable: (optional)
    true only, filter out coins that are not sendable, they might be locked in a contract.
    Default is to return sendable and unsendable coins.

coinid: (optional)
    A coinid, to search for a single coin.

amount: (optional)
    The coin value to search for.

address: (optional)
    Address of a coin to search for, could be a script address.
    Can be a 0x or Mx address.

tokenid: (optional)
    A tokenid, to search for coins of a specific token. Minima is 0x00.

checkmempool: (optional)
    Check if the coin is in the mempool.

coinage: (optional)
    How old does the coin have to be.

depth: (optional)
    How many blocks back to check from Blockchain tip.

order: (optional)
    Order asc or desc (Ascending or Decending).

megammr: (optional)
    Search the MegaMMR for coins too.

simplestate: (optional)
    true or false, default false. Return each coin's state as a simple
    {port:value} object instead of the full typed list.

totalamount: (optional)
    Return just enough of the matching coins to cover this amount, chosen with the
    same coin selection as send. In token units when tokenid is set.

state: (optional)
    Only return coins whose state variables contain this value.

Examples:

coins

coins relevant:true sendable:true

coins relevant:true amount:10

coins coinid:0xEECD7..

coins relevant:true tokenid:0xFED5..

coins relevant:true address:0xCEF6.. tokenid:0x00

coins relevant:true address:MxABC9..

consolidate.help: [tokenid:] (coinage:) (maxcoins:) (maxsigs:) (burn:) (debug:true|false) (dryrun:true|false) (password:) - Consolidate coins by sending them back to yourself
consolidate.fullhelp:
consolidate

Consolidate multiple coins (UTxOs) into one by sending them back to yourself. Must have at least 3 coins.

Useful to prevent having many coins of tiny value and to manage the number of coins you are tracking.

Optionally set the minimum coin age (in blocks), maximum number of coins and maximum number of signatures for the transaction.

tokenid:
    The tokenid for Minima or custom token to consolidate coins for. Minima is 0x00.

coinage: (optional)
    The minimum number of blocks deep (confirmations) a coin needs to be. Default is 3.

maxcoins: (optional)
    The maximum number of coins to consolidate. Minimum 3, up to 20.
    Coins are first sorted by value (smallest first) before adding to the transaction.

maxsigs: (optional)
    The maximum number of signatures for the transaction, up to 5.
    Coins are then sorted by address to minimize the number of signatures required.

burn: (optional)
    Amount of Minima to burn with the transaction.

debug: (optional)
    true or false, true will print more detailed logs.

dryrun: (optional)
    true or false, true will simulate the consolidate transaction but not execute it.

password: (optional)
    If your Wallet is password locked you can unlock it for this one transaction - then relock it.
 
Examples:

consolidate tokenid:0x00

consolidate tokenid:0x77.. coinage:10

consolidate tokenid:0x00 maxcoins:5 password:your_password

consolidate tokenid:0x00 coinage:10 maxcoins:8 burn:1

consolidate tokenid:0x00 coinage:10 maxcoins:8 maxsigs:3 burn:1 dryrun:true

consolidatefrom.help: [fromaddress:] (tokenid:) [script:] [privatekey:] [keyuses:] (mine:true|false) (burn:) (maxcoins:) - Send Minima or Tokens from a certain address
consolidatefrom.fullhelp:
consolidatefrom

Consolidate the coins held at a specific address into one coin, signing with a private
key you supply.

fromaddress:
    The address whose coins are consolidated (Mx.. or 0x..).

script:
    The full KISS VM script of fromaddress, e.g. RETURN SIGNEDBY(0x..)

privatekey:
    The 0x private key seed that signs for fromaddress.

keyuses:
    How many times this private key has already signed. Every signature must use a
    fresh leaf of the key tree, so increase this by one for each signature you make.

tokenid: (optional)
    The token to consolidate. Default 0x00 (Minima).

mine: (optional)
    true or false, default true. Mine the transaction immediately.

burn: (optional)
    The amount of Minima to burn with this transaction.

maxcoins: (optional)
    Maximum number of coins to consolidate in one transaction. Default 50.

Examples:

consolidatefrom fromaddress:Mx.. script:"RETURN SIGNEDBY(0x..)" privatekey:0x.. keyuses:7

consolidatefrom fromaddress:Mx.. tokenid:0x.. script:"RETURN SIGNEDBY(0x..)" privatekey:0x.. keyuses:8 maxcoins:20

multisig.fullhelp:
multisig

Create a multisig coin that can only be used in a txn signed by root OR n of m given public keys.

Can provide the Vault password to temporarily decrypt the private keys when creating the coin or signing a transaction.

action: 
    create : create a new multisig coin.
    getkey : returns one of your default public keys to be provided when creating the coin.
    list : lists all existing multisig coins.
    spend : creates an unsigned transaction (.txn) file to spend a specified amount of a multisig coin.
    sign : signs a multisig transaction (.txn) file with the relevant public keys and outputs a new signed file.
    post : posts the transaction to the network, must be signed as required by the contract before posting.
    view : view the details of a multisig transaction file.

id: (optional)
    Create a multisig coin with an id or list by id.
    Should be unique. This cannot be retrieved later.
    The id is hashed and stored as state variable 0.

amount: (optional)

publickeys: (optional)

required: (optional)

mysql.help: [action:info|setlogin|clearlogin|integrity|update|autobackup|resync|wipe|addresscheck|h2import|h2export|size|rawexport|rawimport|reset|fixmissing|findtxpow] [host:] [database:] [user:] [password:] (keys:) (keyuses:) (phrase:) (address:) (txpowid:) (enable:true|false) (file:) (statecheck:) [logs:true|false] (maxexport:) [readonly:true|false] (startfix:) (endfix:) (block:) - Store and resync the archive data in a MySQL database
mysql.fullhelp:
mysql

Export archive data to a MySQL server.

The MySQL db can be used to perform a chain re-sync to put users on the correct chain,

or a seed re-sync to restore access to lost funds, using the seed phrase.

Can query an address for its history of spent and unspent coins.

Additionally export the MySQL db to a gzip file for resyncing with 'reset' or 'archive' command.

You can use setlogin to auto set the login details
host:
    The ip:port (or name of Docker container) running the MySQL db.

database:
    name of the MySQL db being used to store the archive db data.

user:
    MySQL user to login to as.

password:
    MySQL password for the user provided.

readonly:
    true or false, Connect in readonly mode.
logs:
    Show detailed logs - default true.

action:
    info : Show the blocks stored in the archive db and compare to the MySQL db.
    integrity : Check the block order and block parents are correct in the MySQL db.
    update : Update the MySQL db with the latest syncblocks from the node's archive db.
    addresscheck : Check the history of all the spent and unspent coins from an address.
    setlogin : Set the MySQL login details so you don't need to type them in every time.
    clearlogin : Clear MySQL login details.
    autobackup : Automatically save archive data to MySQL DB. Use with enable. Also stores all TxPoW the node sees.
    findtxpow : Search for an individual TxPoW (only works if autobackup is enabled).
    resync : Perform a chain or seed re-sync from the specified MySQL db.
             Will shutdown the node so you must restart it once complete.
    wipe :  Be careful. Wipe the MySQL db.
    h2export : export the MySQL db to an archive gzip file which can be used to resync a node.
    h2import : import an archive gzip file to the MySQL db.
    rawexport : export the MySQL db to raw.dat file which can be used to resync a node (faster than H2).
    rawimport : import a raw.dat to the MySQL db.
    size : Show the number of blocks stored in the MySQL db.
    reset : Import a raw .dat archive file (file:) into the MySQL db, then re-sync the node from it.
    fixmissing : Scan a raw archive file (file:) and insert any blocks missing from the MySQL db. Use startfix: to skip ahead.

phrase: (optional)
     Use with action:resync. The 24 word seed phrase of the node to re-sync.
     If provided, the node will be wiped and re-synced.
     If not provided, the node will be re-synced to the chain and will not be wiped.

keys: (optional)
    If the seed phrase is provided, optionally set the number of keys to create.
    Default is 80.

keyuses: (optional)
    If the seed phrase is provided, optionally set the number of previous uses for each key created.
    Default is 1000.

address: (optional)
    Use with action:addresscheck. The address to check the history of spent and unspent coins for.

enable: (optional)
    Use with action:autobackup. Automatically save data to MySQL archive DB.

file: (optional)
    Name or path of the archive gzip file to export to or import from.

txpowid: (optional)
    Use with action:findtxpow. The TxPoW id to look up.

statecheck: (optional)
    Use with action:addresscheck. Only include coins whose state variables contain this value.

maxexport: (optional)
    Use with action:rawexport. Maximum number of blocks to export.

startfix: (optional)
    Use with action:fixmissing. The block number to start checking from.

endfix: (optional)
    Accepted but currently unused.

block: (optional)
    Use with action:findtxpow. Look up the block at this block number instead of a TxPoW id.

Examples:

mysql ..LOGIN_DETAILS.. action:setlogin

mysql host:mysqlhost:port database:archivedb user:archiveuser password:archivepassword action:info

mysql host:dockermysql database:archivedb user:archiveuser password:archivepassword action:info

mysql (If you have not setlogin)..LOGIN_DETAILS.. action:integrity

mysql action:update

mysql action:addresscheck address:MxG08.. 

mysql action:resync

mysql action:findtxpow txpowid:0x00FFEEDD..

mysql action:resync phrase:"24 WORDS HERE" keys:90 keyuses:2000

mysql action:rawexport file:archivexport-DDMMYY.gzip

mysql action:size

mysql action:findtxpow block:12345

mysql action:addresscheck address:MxG08.. statecheck:0xFFEEDD..

mysql action:fixmissing file:archivebackup.raw.dat startfix:100000

    chainsync: Re-sync all blocks from the archivefile to get back onto the right chain.

    seedsync: Wipe the wallet and re-generate your keys from your seed phrase. Your coins will be restored.
    restore: Restore a backup and re-sync the entire chain from the archivefile.

file:
    Specify the filename or local path of the backup to restore

password: (optional)

send.fullhelp:

amount: (optional)
    The amount of Minima or custom tokens to send to the specified address.

coinage: (optional)

debug: (optional)
    true or false, true will print more detailed logs.

dryrun: (optional)
    true or false, true will simulate the send transaction but not execute it.

mine: (optional)

fromaddress: (optional)

address:
    The address to send to.

tokenid: (optional)
    The token to send. Default 0x00 (Minima).

sign: (optional)
    true or false, default false. Sign the transaction once it is built.

burn: (optional)
    The amount of Minima to burn with this transaction.

mmrscript: (optional)
    true or false, default true. Add the MMR proofs and scripts for the inputs.

Examples:

txnauto id:mytxn amount:10 address:Mx..

txnauto id:mytxn amount:10 address:Mx.. tokenid:0x.. sign:true

txnbasics.help: (id:) - Automatically set the MMR proofs and scripts for a txn
txnbasics.fullhelp:
txnbasics

Automatically set the MMR proofs and scripts for a transaction.

Only run this when a transaction is ready to be posted.

id:
    The id of the transaction.

Examples:

txnbasics id:simpletxn

txncheck.fullhelp:
txncheck

Show details about the transaction.

Verify whether the inputs, outputs, signatures, proofs and scripts are valid.

id: (optional)
    The id of the transaction to check.

Examples:

txncheck id:multisig

txnclear.fullhelp:
txnclear

Clear the Witness data - signatures, mmr proofs and script proofs.

id:
    The id of the transaction to clear.

scripts:
    Clear the scripts (default : true).

mmr:
    Clear the MMR proofs (default : true).

signatures:
    Clear the signatures (default : true).

Examples:

txnclear id:multisig

txncoinlock.help: (action:lock|unlock) - Lock coins used in un-broadcast transactions
txncoinlock.fullhelp:
txncoinlock

Lock coins used in un-broadcast transactions.


action: (optional)
    lock - lock coins.
    unlock - unlock coins.

Examples:

txncoinlock

txncoinlock action:lock

txncoinlock action:unlock

txncreate.fullhelp:
txncreate

Create a custom transaction.

The first step before defining the inputs and outputs.

id:
    Create an id for the transaction.

Examples:

txncreate id:multisig

txndelete.fullhelp:
txndelete

Delete a previously created custom transaction.

id:

txnexport.help: [id:] (file:) (showtxn:true|false) - Export a transaction as HEX or to a file
txnexport.fullhelp:
txnexport

Export a transaction as HEX or to a file.

The output can then be imported using 'txnimport' to another node. E.g. For signing.

id:
    The id of the transaction to export.

file: (optional)
    File name/path to export the transaction to, must use the .txn extension.

showtxn: (optional)
    true or false, default false. Include the transaction JSON in the response as
    well as the export data.

Examples:

txnexport id:simpletxn

txnexport id:multisig file:multisig.txn

txnimport.help: (id:) (file:) (data:) - Import a transaction as a file or HEX data. Optionally specify the ID
txnimport.fullhelp:
txnimport

Import a transaction from previously exported HEX data or a .txn file.

Optionally specify an ID to use for the new transaction.

id: (optional)
    Choose an ID for the transaction you are importing.

file: (optional)
    File name/path to the previously exported .txn file.

data: (optional)
    HEX data of the previously exported transaction.

Examples:

txnimport data:0x0000..

txnimport id:simpletxn data:0x0000..

txnimport id:multisig file:multisig.txn

txninput.help: [id:] (coinid:) (coindata:) (floating:true|false) (address:) (amount:) (tokenid:) (scriptmmr:true|false) - Add a coin as an input to a transaction
txninput.fullhelp:
txninput

Add a coin as an input to a transaction.

Optionally specify address, amount and tokenid to use an unspecified coinid - a floating ELTOO coin.

A floating coin can be attached to multiple different existing coins as long as it has the same

address, amount and tokenid - but different coinid.

id:
    The id of the transaction to add an input to.

coinid: (optional)
    The id of the coin to add as an input.

coindata: (optional)
    The data of the coin to add, instead of coinid.
    Can be from the 'coinexport' command or 'outputcoindata' from another transaction.

floating: (optional)
    true or false, true will add an unspecified, floating ELTOO coin as an input.
    If true, also specify address, amount, tokenid.
    If false, specify a coinid or coindata.

address: (optional)
    Coin address to use for the floating input. Can be 0x or Mx address.
    The coin that is used 
amount: (optional)
    Amount of a coin for the floating input.

tokenid: (optional)
    tokenid of a coin for the floating input.

scriptmmr: (optional)
    true or false, true will add the scripts and MMR proof for the coin.

Examples:

txninput id:simpletxn coinid:0xD0BF..

txninput id:multisig coinid:0xD0BF.. scriptmmr:true

txninput id:posttxn coindata:0x000..

txninput id:eltootxn floating:true address:0xFED5.. amount:10 tokenid:0x00

txnlist.fullhelp:
txnlist

List your custom transactions. Includes previously posted transactions.

Returns the full details of transactions.

id: (optional)
    The id of a single transaction to list.

transactiononly: (optional)
    true or false, default false. Return only the transaction itself, without the
    witness and the other row details.

Examples:

txnlist

txnlist id:multisig

txnlock.help: (action:lock|unlock|list) (timeout:) (unlockdelay:) - Gain a lock. Stops multiple txnfunctions occuring simultaneously
txnlock.fullhelp:
txnlock

When creating multiple transactions asynchronously you can ensure each is created one at a time.

action:
    lock - Gain a lock
    unlock - Release lock
    list/blank - Are we locked

timeout:
    How long to wait for the lock

unlockdelay:
    Wait this amount of milli after unlock.

Examples:

txnlock

txnlock action:lock timeout:10000

txnlock action:unlock unlockdelay:5000

txnmine.help: (id:) (data:) - Mine a txn but don't post it from either ID or txnexport Data
txnmine.fullhelp:
txnmine

Mine a transaction without posting it, from a stored transaction (id:) or from exported
transaction data (data:).

Post the mined result later with txnminepost.

id: (optional)
    The id of a stored transaction to mine.

data: (optional)
    Exported transaction data (from txnexport) to mine instead of a stored id.

Examples:

txnmine id:mytxn

txnmine data:0x..

txnminepost.fullhelp:
txnminepost

Post a transaction that was pre-mined with txnmine.

data:
    The pre-mined transaction data returned by txnmine.

Examples:

txnminepost data:0x..

txnmmr.help: (id:) - Add MMR proofs to a transaction leaving those already present
txnmmr.fullhelp:
txnmmr

Add the MMR proofs to every input of a transaction that does not already have one.

id:
    The transaction id.

Examples:

txnmmr id:mytxn

txnoutput.fullhelp:
txnoutput

Create a transaction output.

This will create a new coin (UTxO).

If the sum of inputs > outputs, the difference will be burned unless change to the sender is defined as an output.

Optionally store the transaction state variables in the new output coin.

id:
    The id of the transaction to add an output to.

amount:
    The amount for the output. To send to the specified address.

address:
    Address of the recipient/script to send the output to. Can be 0x or Mx address.

tokenid: (optional)
    tokenid of the output. Default is Minima (0x00).

storestate: (optional)
    true or false, true will keep the state variables of the transaction in the newly created output coin.
    Default is true.

Examples:

txnoutput id:simpletxn amount:10 address:0xFED5..

txnoutput id:multisig amount:10 address:0xFED5.. tokenid:0xCEF5.. storestate:false

txnoutput id:eltootxn amount:10 address:0xFED5..

txnpost.help: [id:] (auto:true|false) (burn:) (mine:true|false) (txndelete:true|false) - Post a transaction. Automatically set the Scripts and MMR
txnpost.fullhelp:
txnpost

Post a transaction. Automatically set the Scripts and MMR proofs.

Optionally set a burn for the transaction.

id:
    The id of the transaction.

auto: (optional)
    Set the scripts and MMR proofs for the transaction.

burn: (optional)
    Amount in Minima to burn with the transaction.

mine: (optional)
    true or false - should you mine the transaction immediately.

txndelete: (optional)
    true or false - delete this txn after posting.

Examples:

txnpost id:simpletxn

txnpost id:simpletxn auto:true burn:0.1

txnpost id:multisig burn:0.1

txnscript.fullhelp:
txnscript

Add scripts to a transaction.

id:
    The id of the transaction.

auto:
    Automatically add scripts you know. Useful for multi user transactions.

scripts:
    JSON holds the script and the proof in the format {script:proof}
    If it is a single script, and not one created with mmrcreate, leave the proof blank.
    If it is an mmrcreate script, include the proof.

Examples:

txnscript id:txnmast scripts:{"RETURN TRUE":""}

txnscript id:txnmast scripts:{"RETURN TRUE":"0x000.."}

txnsign.fullhelp:
txnsign

Sign a transaction.

Specify the public key or use 'auto' if the coin inputs are simple.

id:
    The id of the transaction to sign.

publickey:
    The public key specified in a custom script, or 'auto' for transactions with simple inputs.
    custom : sign with the privatekey: and keyuses: you supply.

txnpostauto: (optional)
    Do you want to post this transaction. Use the same values as you would for txnpost auto(sort MMR and Scripts)

txnpostburn: (optional)
    If you also post this transaction, do you want to add a burn transaction.

txnpostmine: (optional)
    If you also post this transaction, do you want to mine it immediately.

txndelete: (optional)
    true or false - delete this txn after signing AND posting.

password: (optional)
    If your wallet is password locked, unlock it for this signing and relock it afterwards.

privatekey: (optional)
    Use with publickey:custom. The 0x private key seed to sign with.

keyuses: (optional)
    Use with publickey:custom. How many times this private key has already signed. Every signature must use a
    fresh leaf of the key tree, so increase this by one for each signature you make.

Examples:

txnsign id:simpletxn publickey:auto

txnsign id:simpletxn publickey:auto password:your_password

txnsign id:multisig publickey:0xFD8B..

txnsign id:simpletxn publickey:auto txnpostauto:true

txnsign id:multisig publickey:custom privatekey:0x.. keyuses:5

txnstate.fullhelp:
txnstate

Add a state variable to a transaction.

id:
    The id of the transaction.

port:
    Port number of the state variable, from 0-255.

value:
    Value for the state variable.

Examples:

txnstate id:multisig port:0 value:0xFED5..

txnstate id:multisig port:1 value:100 

txnstate id:multisig port:1 value:"string"

txnview.help: (file:) (data:) - View a transaction as a JSON.
txnview.fullhelp:
txnimport

View a transaction from previously exported HEX data or a .txn file.

file: (optional)
    File name/path to the previously exported .txn file.

data: (optional)
    HEX data of the previously exported transaction.

Examples:

txnview data:0x0000..

txpow.help: (txpowid:) (block:) (address:) (onchain:) (relevant:true) (max:) (action:info) (inblock:) - Search for a specific TxPoW or check for onchain
txpow.fullhelp:
txpow

Search for a specific TxPoW in the unpruned chain or your mempool.

Search by txpowid, block or 0x / Mx address.

txpowid: (optional)
    TxPoW id of the TxPoW to search for.
    Returns the txpow details.

onchain: (optional)
    TxPoW id to search for on chain. Must be in the unpruned chain.
    Returns block info and number of confirmations.

block: (optional)
    Block number to search in. Must be in the unpruned chain.

address: (optional)
    0x or Mx address. Search for TxPoWs containing this specific address.

relevant: (optional)
    true or false. Only list TxPoWs relevant to this node.

max: (optional)
    Max relevant TxPoW to retrieve. Default 100.

action: (optional)
    info : Show the TxPoW database details - stored days, SQL size and the
           on-chain DB size with its first and last block.

inblock: (optional)
    A block number, or a block's txpowid (0x..). List the TxPoW IDs included in
    that block, from the on-chain DB.

Examples:

txpow txpowid:0x000..

txpow block:200

txpow address:0xCEF6..

txpow onchain:0x000..

txpow action:info

txpow inblock:12345

txpow inblock:0x000..

vault.help: (action:seed|wipekeys|restorekeys|passwordlock|passwordunlock|testphrase|resetkeys) (seed:) (keyuses:) (phrase:) (password:) (confirm:) (numkeys:) - BE CAREFUL. Wipe/Restore/Encrypt/Decrypt your private keys
vault.fullhelp:
vault

BE CAREFUL. Wipe / Restore your private keys.

View your passphrase and seed. DO NOT SHARE THESE WITH ANYONE.

ENSURE YOU HAVE A BACKUP AND SECURE RECORD OF YOUR PASSPHRASE BEFORE LOCKING.

You must have your passphrase to unlock your private keys.

action: (optional)
    seed : Show your seed phrase. The default. 
    wipekeys : Wipe your private keys - keep the public.
    restorekeys : Restore your private keys.
    passwordlock : Lock your node by password encrypting private keys.
    passwordunlock : Unlock your node to reinstating your private keys.
    testphrase : Derive the seed and the first numkeys public keys / addresses from a phrase, to check it. Does not touch your wallet.
    resetkeys : BE CAREFUL. Wipe the chain, TxPoW and wallet databases and regenerate every key from the phrase (with keyuses: previous uses).

seed: (optional)
    Enter your seed to lock your node.
    This will delete your private keys.

phrase: (optional)
    Enter your passphrase in double quotes to restore your node.
    This will reinstate your private keys.

keyuses: (optional)
    Use with action:resetkeys. The number of previous uses to assume for every key.
    Default 100.

password: (optional)
    Use with action:passwordlock or action:passwordunlock. The password that
    encrypts / decrypts your private keys. It cannot contain ;

confirm: (optional)
    Use with action:passwordlock. Must match password: exactly or the lock is refused.

numkeys: (optional)
    Use with action:testphrase. How many keys and addresses to derive from the
    phrase. Default 4.

Examples:

vault

vault action:wipekeys seed:0xDD4E..

vault action:restorekeys phrase:"SPRAY LAMP.."

vault action:passwordlock password:your_password

vault action:passwordlock password:your_password confirm:your_password

vault action:passwordunlock password:your_password

vault action:testphrase phrase:"SPRAY LAMP.." numkeys:8

vault action:resetkeys phrase:"SPRAY LAMP.." keyuses:1000

verify.fullhelp:
verify

Verify a signature. Returns valid true or false.

data:
    The 0x HEX data to verify the signature for.

publickey:
    The public key of the signer.

signature:
    The signature of the data.

Examples:

verify data:0xCD34.. publickey:0xFED5 signature:0x4827..

webhooks.help: (enable:true|false) (action:list|add|remove|clear|errorlogs) (hook:) (filter:) - Add a web hook that is called with Minima events as they happen
webhooks.fullhelp:
webhooks

Add a web hook that is called with Minima events as they happen.

POST requests, so the URL must be a POST endpoint.

action: (optional)
    list : List your existing webhooks. The default.
    add : Add a new webhook. 
    remove : Remove an existing webhook.
    clear : Clear the existing webhooks.
    errorlogs : Turn logging of webhook delivery errors on or off. Use with enable:true|false.

hook: (optional)
    A URL, must be a POST endpoint.

filter: (optional)
    Filters which events get posted.

enable: (optional)
    true or false. Use with action:errorlogs to turn logging of failed webhook calls
    on or off.

Examples:

webhooks action:list

webhooks action:add hook:http://127.0.0.1/myapi.php

webhooks action:remove hook:http://127.0.0.1/myapi.php

webhooks action:add hook:http://127.0.0.1/myapi.php filter:MINING

webhooks action:clear

webhooks action:errorlogs enable:true
